title: Precision-swing Workshop: latency/fidelity matrix & profile heatmap
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Helios through the Optimize console heatmap, showing INT8 vs FP8 profile selections across throughput/latency slices. Discussed fidelity metrics, sample prompt sets, KV cache/ prefix caching impact, and a pilot benchmark plan. Team aligned on running a 2-week sandbox with 3 model variants (FP16 baseline, FP8 profile, INT8 aggressive) and agreed next steps: security docs, sandbox creds, and schedule of bench run.
topics: INT8 vs FP8 tradeoffs (quality delta vs latency gains)
Console heatmap visualization and how profiles map to latency targets
Batching, KV cache effects, and autoscaling implications
Pilot/pricing and success criteria for sandbox benchmark
next_steps: Redwood to send pilot pricing sheet and sandbox onboarding link (by 2026-08-24)
Helios to provide 200 representative prompts and pass/fail criteria (by 2026-08-27)
Schedule bench kickoff meeting for week of 2026-08-31
action_items: Maya Chen: Share Optimize heatmap export and quant-profile spreadsheet; Due: 2026-08-24
Owen Park: Provision sandbox and create test harness template; Due: 2026-08-25
Priya Nair: Collect 200 sample prompts and baseline metrics from current infra; Due: 2026-08-27
Marcus Li: Provide network/VPN requirements and SSO contact for private pilot; Due: 2026-08-26
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're—uh—running a focused walkthrough of Optimize's profile heatmap and how you can pick INT8/FP8 profiles based on your latency SLOs. Marcus, Priya, you good on the audio?
[00:12] Priya (Helios): Yep, sounds good. we have Sofia on as well. thanks for doing this on short notice.
[00:18] Marcus (Helios): Morning, all. quick note, our main constraint is 250ms p95 for customer facing responses, and cost per 1M tokens is also a hard budget.
[00:27] Owen (SE): Got it. we'll show how the heatmap maps quality delta to latency gains and give you an apples-to-apples baseline vs FP16. there will be some noise in the transcription—sorry if some product names get munged.
[00:38] Sofia (Helios): that's fine, just want to see tradeoffs.
[00:44] [00:45] Owen (SE): so here's the console, this is the Optimize -> Profiles tab. on the left you see baseline FP16 numbers and on the right a set of candidate profiles. the heatmap is keyed by p95 latency (y axis) and relative quality drop (x axis). warmer colors = larger quality delta.
[01:05] Maya (AE): quick refresher: FP8 generally gives you a good mid ground—most customers see 20-35% token speedups vs FP16 depending on kernel support, INT8 can be 2-3x faster but has more variable quality impact especially on instruction-following and codegen.
[01:24] Priya (Helios): can you quantify "quality"—are you using BLEU/ROUGE or human evals?
[01:30] Owen (SE): Good question. in the demo heatmap we use a composite score: automated evals (ROUGE/Exact match where applicable) plus a small human rating cohort for instruction-following. in your pilot we'd recommend using your own top-200 prompt set and a pass/fail threshold you define.
[01:50] Marcus (Helios): our prompts are mixed: slot-filling, short summarization, and a few code snippets. codegen quality is a big concern.
[01:58] Owen (SE): noted. codegen is sensitive to quantization; INT8 aggressive profiles may need per-layer or per-op mix. the console supports hybrid profiles—so you can keep attention/FFN at FP8 and quantize matmul to INT8, for instance.
[02:17] [02:20] Maya (AE): I want to call out caching effects—KV cache and prefix caching can reduce the number of tokens that need to be generated, so the effective latency gain from quantization is lower for heavy cache workloads. we show that in the heatmap by running two sims: cold start and cached paths.
[02:37] Priya (Helios): that matters, ~70% of our traffic hits cached completions. so maybe int8 isn't worth it?
[02:43] Owen (SE): exactly why we recommend mixed experiments. FP8 often hits your latency SLO without material quality regression when caching is heavy; INT8 shines on cold path and streaming heavy workloads.
[02:56] [03:00] Owen (SE): switching to the profile comparison view—here you can click a cell and see sample outputs side-by-side. you'll see the FP16 baseline, FP8 candidate, and INT8 candidate. notice how the FP8 variant preserves punctuation and instruction-following much better in many examples.
[03:19] Priya (Helios): the side-by-side looks pretty close on the short summarization examples. what about hallucination rate?
[03:25] Owen (SE): we track hallucination heuristics per prompt set; FP8 usually does better than INT8 on hallucination-sensitive tasks. we'll surface those metrics in the bench results.
[03:34] Marcus (Helios): any changes required on our side to run the sandbox? network? auth?
[03:38] Maya (AE): minimal. we'll share a sandbox onboarding doc with a service account and short instructions. if you want a private pilot in your VPC, we'll need your network team and SSO details—Marcus, you mentioned SSO earlier?
[03:51] Marcus (Helios): yes, SSO is on Okta. I'll share the SSO contact offline.
[03:55] [04:00] Owen (SE): talking about latency, here's an interesting piece: when we enable continuous batching, INT8 can reduce per-token latency but increase tail latency for small requests if batching waits to accumulate tokens. Optimize lets you configure latency-targeted batching to avoid that.
[04:21] Priya (Helios): so if we set target p95=250ms, console can suggest profile and batching config?
[04:26] Owen (SE): Yes. the suggestion engine will recommend a profile and a batching window that historically meets your SLO for similar workloads. it's probabilistic, so we suggest benching with your real traffic.
[04:37] [04:45] Maya (AE): quick demo of the suggestion flow: select workload, target latency, importance weight for quality vs cost, then it returns a ranked list of profiles plus expected cost per 1M tokens.
[04:59] Sofia (Helios): how accurate are the cost estimates? we saw big variance with previous vendors.
[05:06] Owen (SE): estimates are based on measured per-token GPU time across our kernel set and include a heuristics layer for batching and cache hit rates. we provide confidence bands and a recommended safety margin. we can also run a short microbench to calibrate to your exact sequences.
[05:21] Priya (Helios): can we run a microbench against our codegen prompts?
[05:24] Owen (SE): Absolutely. that's part of the pilot. we'll spin up three variants and run them against your 200 prompts under two traffic patterns (cached heavy vs cold start).
[05:35] [05:40] Maya (AE): sharing a link in chat to the example heatmap and the quant-profile spreadsheet: https://redwood.link/opt-heatmap-demo and Drive: /shared/Helios/quant-profiles.xlsx
[05:52] Marcus (Helios): got it. one more compliance question: do you keep logs of user inputs? we need to know retention and KMS details.
[05:59] Owen (SE): We have options: hosted mode stores logs with customer-controlled retention and KMS; Dedicated/Private can avoid long-term retention and integrate with your KMS/HSM. we'll send the SOC2 and encryption docs.
[06:12] [06:20] Priya (Helios): curious about rollouts: if FP8 looks good but we worry about edge cases, can we do canary with fallback to FP16?
[06:26] Owen (SE): yes—console supports canary rollouts with automatic fallback rules. you can route only N% of traffic to a profile and set automatic rollback triggers on quality regressions.
[06:36] Maya (AE): ok, demo time: I'm going to trigger a simulated bench run—this is synthetic but illustrates results. running FP16 baseline first.
[06:42] [10:12] [10:15] Owen (SE): baseline completed, p95 310ms for this synthetic workload. now running FP8 profile A—note it has attention at FP8 and FFN at FP8 with selective INT8 matmul.
[10:26] Priya (Helios): that p95 drop looks promising. what's the quality delta?
[10:30] Owen (SE): automatic metric shows -1.8% composite score vs baseline on this sample set. human gold set showed negligible behavioral regressions.
[10:39] [11:00] Maya (AE): now running INT8 aggressive. this will show latency gains but note the quality delta can spike on codegen samples.
[11:10] [14:50] Owen (SE): INT8 p95 for synthetic run is 140ms, quality delta -6.3% on composite. we highlight which prompts degrade—mostly codegen and instruction-following where precision matters.
[14:59] Priya (Helios): that lines up with our worries. if 70% of traffic is cached, effective overall customer-perceived p95 might be lower, so FP8 is probably our sweet spot.
[15:12] Marcus (Helios): cost math—how much are we saving? can you show cost per million tokens?
[15:18] Maya (AE): in the simulation, FP8 reduced compute cost by ~28% vs FP16; INT8 by ~55% but with higher quality risk. we'll send a detailed cost spreadsheet.
[15:30] [15:45] Owen (SE): another point: quantization sensitivity differs by model family and by sequence length. for longer sequences, INT8 tends to amplify errors in attention normalization. Optimize shows sequence-length segmented results so you can pick profiles per-route.
[16:05] Priya (Helios): could we do route-based profiles? e.g., route summarization to FP8, codegen to FP16?
[16:12] Owen (SE): exactly. route-level routing + profile pinning is supported. you can also set automatic fallback for certain routes.
[16:21] [16:30] Sofia (Helios): how long does a bench usually take for 200 prompts? we want results within two weeks.
[16:35] Owen (SE): end-to-end bench (including micro-calibration, warm/cold runs) usually 3-5 days if you provide prompts; with analysis and deck ~7-10 business days. 2 weeks is comfortable.
[16:46] Priya (Helios): ok good. what about instrumentation—how will we detect quality regressions in production?
[16:52] Owen (SE): Redwood has per-prompt regression alerts tied to your seed prompts and policies. you can set thresholds and get a webhook/Slack alert. we also provide token-level diff views and per-route histograms.
[17:05] [17:15] Marcus (Helios): security doc timeline? we need SOC2 reports and encryption at rest details for compliance review next week.
[17:20] Maya (AE): we'll attach SOC2, ISO, encryption, and network diagrams in the onboarding email. expect that by tomorrow EOD.
[17:29] Priya (Helios): for the pilot success criteria—I'd like to propose: maintain <2% drop in composite quality, p95 <=250ms in production-like traffic, cost <= X% vs current baseline.
[17:40] Owen (SE): that sounds reasonable; we'll validate with the bench and refine thresholds per-route.
[17:46] [18:00] Maya (AE): quick Q&A—Sofia, any remaining concerns at the platform level?
[18:05] Sofia (Helios): only that we want clear rollback triggers and SLO guardrails. sounds like you support that.
[18:11] Owen (SE): Yes—canary + auto rollback and config locks via RBAC.
[18:16] [18:30] Maya (AE): wrapping up: I will send the pilot pricing, the shared drive link, and the sandbox onboarding. Owen will provision the sandbox and the bench harness. Priya will collect prompts. Marcus will share Okta contact and network constraints.
[18:44] Priya (Helios): thanks, this was useful.
[18:48] Marcus (Helios): thanks everyone.
[18:50] Sofia (Helios): thanks — looking forward to results.
[18:53] Maya (AE): great, we'll follow up with the items. talk soon.
[18:58] [End of recording]
